content: Halofantrine is an antimalarial agent that acts as a blood schizonticide. It does not exhibit any apparent activity against the sporozoite, gametocyte, or hepatic stages of the malaria infection. The precise mechanism by which halofantrine exerts its antimalarial effects remains unknown. Both the parent compound and its primary metabolite, N-desbutyl halofantrine, demonstrate equivalent activity in vitro. In vitro studies suggest the possibility of cross-resistance between halofantrine and mefloquine. However, clinical data do not support this hypothesis. No significant correlation between resistance to halofantrine and mefloquine was observed in clinical trials. In controlled clinical trials involving 90 non-immune patients with malaria caused by Plasmodium falciparum, treatment with Halfan (500 mg administered every 6 hours for three doses on days 0 and 7) achieved a cure rate of 99%. Patients were monitored for 28 days or longer following the initiation of treatment. In additional trials involving 583 patients with acute malaria, most of whom were semi-immune, treatment with Halfan (500 mg every 6 hours for three doses) resulted in a 90% cure rate for Plasmodium falciparum infections (n = 512) and a 99% cure rate for Plasmodium vivax infections (n = 71).
